title: [office hours · 2026-09-08] Eval sets, noise bands, and why your delta is not real
body:
> **Office hours.** One thread per session. Agenda goes up before, notes go up after, and the
> thread stays open — so the answers are findable by whoever hits the same thing in three months.

**When:** Monday 8 September 2026 · async, all week. Post questions in this thread at any time.

## Agenda

Three things, in order of how often they come up.

**1 · "My change improved the metric — is it real?"**
Walking through [#29](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/discussions/29) end to end: why two
metrics can give opposite verdicts on the same change, why `n_boot` is not `n`, and the
arithmetic for how many eval questions a 2-point delta actually needs. Bring your own numbers.

**2 · "How do I build an eval set when the client has no labels?"**
The most common real blocker. Notebook 02 is the method;
[EX-04](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/30-learning/exercises/ex-04-manufacture-an-eval-set-for-a-new-domain.md)
is the practice. The part people skip is null questions, and skipping them means you cannot
measure abstention at all.

**3 · Open floor.**

## How to get a useful answer

Post the **numbers**, the **config that produced them**, and **what you already tried**. A
question with a measurement in it gets answered in one round trip.

## Notes

Added after the session, in a reply to this thread.

comments.body:
> **Priya** · cohort peer

Question for slot 1, posting early so it is in the queue.

I have a change that clears the band on `evidence_recall` and not on `full_chain_recall`, which
is exactly the #29 case. But my eval set is 96 questions, not 207. Does the ~380 figure from that
thread scale, or does something else break at that size?

replies.body:
> **Dana** · reviewer · owns the eval harness

It scales, and something else does break — worth taking as the first question on the day.

The scaling is `n × (half-width / point-estimate)²`, so run it with your own numbers rather than
borrowing 380.

What breaks at 96 is more interesting: **the bootstrap itself becomes unreliable, not just
wide.** Percentile intervals assume the resampled distribution is a decent stand-in for the
sampling distribution, and at `n < ~100` on a binary metric that assumption gets thin — you are
resampling from very few distinct outcomes. The interval is not merely wide, its *coverage* is
off, so it may not be a true 95% interval at all.

Bring the raw per-question rows and we can look at the resampled distribution directly.
